I read a lot. I would say I have devoured or reread nearly a hundred books already this year. There are many great stories out there. Some are more difficult reads because there are so many characters, a plot takes many different turns, or any other number of possible problems. Some are great for these same reasons. What inspired me to make this post was the realization of how certain books touch us in a way that elicits an emotional response. Very few writers have managed to touch me in that way and then only once or twice in an entire series. There is one writer however that has managed to do this to me several times in each of many of the books they have written.

 

I would just like to say if you haven't read any of Robin Hobb's work with Fitz, Nighteyes, and the Fool, you should.

 

I read the first of those books years ago and the characters feel like old friends. I want to go back and read these again now that I am partially through the latest book but I don't really want to experience some of the emotions again. I will though.

 

Are there any others out there that touch you in the same way?
Not many have made me shed a tear.

I know the feeling that you are talking about and while I read more than my fair share of books, I am still waiting to get that set of feelings from an author. I usually get those feelings from music, particularly music that reminds me of my childhood or very important personal relationships like my parents or siblings.
Please if you could offer me up a reading list of books that have hit you I would like to perhaps read them if I already havent, I would love to experiance that reaction from reading though.
Flowers for Algernon by Daniel Keyes have a special place in my heart. It's more of a science fiction book though.

I don't want to read past the third book, because i've formed a presumptuous version of the story that i suspect may be violated later on. It's somewhat of a habit i've developed when reading this sort of fiction. It's hard to go back to the world when it's not quite how you remember it, and you want it to be.
